blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Some regions in the Philippines have so few occupational therapists and speech-language pathologists that a single professional is expected to serve the needs of thousands — in some cases, as many as 16,000 — learners with disabilities. The Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom 2) pointed this out as it identified, together with government representatives and health professionals, priority areas where access to assessment and intervention services can be improved. Based on data presented by Edcom 2, there are only two occupational therapists for an estimated 24,160 learners in Bicol, equivalent to one occupational therapist for every 12,080 […]...
